title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten Center City corridors near Jefferson’s Philadelphia campus, each anchored by a named, publicly documented destination.

cards.title: Arch Street: Reading Terminal Market
cards.subtitle: Arch Street corridor — Reading Terminal Market at 12th Street
cards.notes: Enter from Arch Street and use the market’s official directory to choose one vendor or browse the public-market aisles before heading back to campus.
cards.short_summary: A historic indoor public market with more than 80 merchants.
cards.evidence_claim: Reading Terminal Market is at 51 N. 12th Street and has more than 80 merchants.
cards.source_title: Reading Terminal Market: America's Best Public Market
cards.access_notes: Check the market’s official website for current vendor and building hours.

cards.title: Arch Street: Pennsylvania Convention Center
cards.subtitle: Arch Street corridor — Pennsylvania Convention Center at 11th Street
cards.notes: Walk the Arch Street frontage to see the convention center’s scale, then check its official calendar before planning around a public event.
cards.short_summary: A six-block convention complex with an Arch Street entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pennsylvania Convention Center is at 1101 Arch Street; its Arch Street entrance leads toward Reading Terminal Market and the historic district.
cards.access_notes: Public access depends on scheduled events; consult the center’s official calendar and event policies.

cards.title: Market Street: Fashion District Philadelphia
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — Fashion District at 9th Street
cards.notes: Use the Market Street entrance, then consult the official directory for current shops, food counters, entertainment, and accessibility details.
cards.short_summary: A three-block indoor retail and entertainment destination on East Market.
cards.evidence_claim: Fashion District Philadelphia is at 901 Market Street and spans three city blocks along East Market Street.
cards.access_notes: Official visitor information lists variable hours; verify current hours before going.

cards.title: North Broad Street: Masonic Temple
cards.subtitle: North Broad Street corridor — Masonic Temple at City Hall
cards.notes: Photograph the landmark exterior from Broad Street, or reserve a guided tour through the official site to see its historic interiors.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark housing the Masonic Library and Museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Masonic Temple at One North Broad Street is a National Historic Landmark and home to the Masonic Library and Museum.
cards.access_notes: Guided tours and admission are offered through the official site; availability may vary.

cards.title: South 15th Street: Dilworth Park
cards.subtitle: South 15th Street corridor — Dilworth Park beside City Hall
cards.notes: Use the seating and pedestrian space as a pause point, then check the official park calendar for seasonal performances or recreation programming.
cards.short_summary: A City Hall public space with a programmable fountain and seasonal uses.
cards.evidence_claim: Dilworth Park is at 1 S. 15th Street and includes a programmable fountain, lawns, seating, and seasonal programming.
cards.access_notes: The park is outdoors; seasonal activities and event access vary. Check the official calendar.

cards.entity_name: LOVE Park / John F. Kennedy Plaza
cards.title: JFK Boulevard: LOVE Park
cards.subtitle: John F. Kennedy Boulevard corridor — LOVE Park at 15th Street
cards.notes: Stop at the LOVE sculpture on the park’s east side, then use the City’s park information to confirm any current public programming.
cards.short_summary: A civic plaza documented by the City as the site of the LOVE sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies LOVE Park / John F. Kennedy Plaza at 1501 John F. Kennedy Boulevard and places the LOVE sculpture on its eastern side.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public park; organized activities may require reservations or permits.

cards.title: Arch Street: African American Museum
cards.subtitle: Arch Street corridor — African American Museum in Philadelphia at 7th Street
cards.notes: Use the museum’s current exhibition listings to plan a visit, and pause outside to view the documented public sculptures at the building.
cards.short_summary: A museum interpreting African American history and culture in Philadelphia.
cards.evidence_claim: The African American Museum in Philadelphia is at 701 Arch Street and was founded in 1976 to preserve, interpret, and exhibit African American heritage and culture.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and exhibition access are subject to its current visitor policies.

cards.title: Arch Street: National Constitution Center
cards.subtitle: Arch Street corridor — National Constitution Center at 5th Street
cards.notes: Plan around the museum’s official daily schedule and pick an exhibit or live program before walking east through Independence National Historical Park.
cards.short_summary: A museum and civic education center focused on the U.S. Constitution.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Constitution Center is an interactive museum, national town hall, and civic education headquarters at 525 Arch Street.
cards.access_notes: Official visitor information lists daily museum hours; admission is ticketed.

cards.title: South 22nd Street: Mütter Museum
cards.subtitle: South 22nd Street corridor — Mütter Museum near Market Street
cards.notes: Review the museum’s current exhibition guidance before visiting, especially if medical-history collections may not suit everyone in your group.
cards.short_summary: A medical-history museum with collections of anatomical and pathological materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mütter Museum is at 19 S. 22nd Street and its collection includes bones, plaster casts, medical illustrations, and pathological specimens.
cards.access_notes: Admission and visitor guidance are set by the museum; review its official website before going.

cards.title: North 6th Street: Franklin Square
cards.subtitle: North 6th Street corridor — Franklin Square at Race Street
cards.notes: Walk the square’s paths and fountain area, then check the official operator’s calendar for any seasonal light show or family programming.
cards.short_summary: A public square with a historic fountain, green space, and seasonal attractions.
cards.evidence_claim: Franklin Square is at 200 N. 6th Street and includes green space, a carousel, playgrounds, and the Franklin Square Fountain.
cards.source_title: Your Guide to the 25 Best Parks in Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: The outdoor square is publicly accessible; individual attractions and seasonal programming may charge admission.
